There is precedent for swapping a given set of barrels that the US government has received in-kind for the medium-sour barrels that typically fill the SPR.

But otherwise these will need to be sold off to refineries—and Washington pockets the difference between cost and market $?

Hmm. It’s going to be very interesting to watch how this turns out.

Most people familiar with the SPR have long known that Venezuelan heavy crude (and Canadian dilbit) isn’t suitable for the SPR because of quality incompatibility and separation issues.

But that isn’t to say you CANNOT shove this type of crude into the reserves—just that it’s not advisable and will likely cause issues in the future.

Maybe this is less of an issue today given that some of the caverns are now effectively empty (less incompatibility issues with current holdings) or maybe the Trump admin just won’t care about future issues and shove it in there anyway 🤷🏻‍♂️

Based on this Reuters report, sounds like we’ll be finding out sooner than later.
